content.description:
Netflix (NFLX) reported fourth-quarter earnings of $0.56 per share. Revenue was $12.05 billion versus an estimate of $11.97 billion. For the first quarter, the streaming giant sees earnings of $0.76 per share and revenue of $12.16 billion.

Netflix also announced it will suspend stock buybacks to help fund its purchase of Warner Bros.

content.title: Netflix Stock Is Falling. This Is Overshadowing the Streamer’s Earnings Beat.
content.summary: Netflix  issued softer-than-expected margin guidance late Tuesday, overshadowing higher fourth-quarter earnings than expected.  The video streamer reported a fourth-quarter profit of 56 cents a share, as revenue climbed almost 18% from a year ago to $12.05 billion.  Analysts were looking for earnings of 55 cents a share on revenue of $11.97 billion, according to FactSet.

content.title: Netflix Issues Cautious Forecast Amid WBD Saga
content.description: John Belton of Gabelli Funds reacts to Netflix's fourth-quarter earnings on "Bloomberg The Close." He says the top-line numbers look generally healthy, but margin guidance is disappointing. The streaming leader says it plans to increase spending on films and TV shows by 10% in 2026 while forging ahead with plans to buy the studio and streaming business of Warner Bros. Discovery.

content.title: Netflix delivers solid 4th quarter, but stock sinks amid worries about slowing subscriber growth
content.summary: Netflix capped last year with another solid financial performance despite slowing subscriber growth that underscored the importance of its contested $72 billion bid to take over Warner Bros.’ movie studio and slot HBO Max into its video streaming line-up.  The fourth-quarter results announced Tuesday eclipsed the projections of stock market analysts, but Netflix's report also noted that the video service ended the year with more than 325 million worldwide subscribers, a figure indicating it has added about 23 million subscribers since 2024.  The 2025 subscriber increase marked a dramatic slowdown from the 41 million picked up during 2024, amplifying investor worries that Netflix's growth has peaked since the 2022 introduction of a low-priced, advertising-supported version of its service that triggered a massive surge in subscribers.
